descriptive: Sides named as built (reuse side, new side); no reuse/new verdict. The user's expectation (2026-11-17: 'Expected: the reuse side reads higher') is filed as P1/P2 below and read descriptively.
question: On the nine 67M built pairs, as built and size-matched, is the base-vs-fine-tune activation change at block 2's input carried more by crosscoder latents the base model also has (shared) than by latents only the fine-tune has (fine-tune-specific after latent scaling), on the side built to reuse than on the side built to be new?

sources.expansion, k, lr, init_norm, paired init: Minder et al. 2025 App. K, Table 3 (32x, k 100, lr 1e-4, BatchTopK init norm 1.0)
sources.epochs: Minder et al. 2025 Table 3 (BatchTopK crosscoder, 2 epochs)
sources.activation scale: one scalar for both models setting the base mean norm to sqrt(d) (Anthropic, 'Training Sparse Autoencoders', Circuits Updates April 2024); not stated by Minder et al.
sources.theta: Minder et al. 2025 eqs. 13-14 (mean over training batches of the smallest selected value); here the last 10% of steps
sources.shared, ft_only, base_only: Minder et al. 2025 Table 4 (0.4-0.6, 0.9-1.0, 0-0.1), from Lindsey et al. 2024's relative norm
sources.nu_r, nu_eps: Minder et al. 2025 glossary: chat-specific = nu_r < 0.5 and nu_eps < 0.2
sources.layer: Lindsey et al. 2024 and Minder et al. 2025: the middle layer's residual; block 2's input is after 2 of 4 blocks
sources.batch, dead_tokens, alive_min, task_frac: not given in the sources; chosen here and listed as departures in the plan

expected.self (base against itself): activations equal (max abs 0); every alive latent's relative norm 0.5 (exact by the paired init and equal inputs); 0 fine-tune-only latents; FVE about 0.85 (Minder's 0.87 at k 100 on a 2304-wide model; bar 0.5); the change reading undefined (no change): nan
expected.planted (one new direction at the answer: 1 to 3 fine-tune-specific latents; fine-tune-specific part 0.7 to 0.9 (bar 0.5); d about -0.8
expected.random update at the reuse state's per-m: d near 0 (|d| < 0.2); the error part at least 0.5 (a random change has no dictionary of its own); no bar, reported
expected.e54_matched seed 0: rival A: d about +0.3 on the reuse state (elicit), about 0 on the new state (cipher); rival B: within 0.1 of each other
expected.built pairs: rival A: gap > 0 on at least 7 of 9, apart on at least 5; rival B: gap inside the seed ranges on at least 7 of 9

rules.d: per side: d = shared part - fine-tune-specific part of the change on the task's score-half windows (commute.crosscoder.change_parts); nan when the change energy is 0
rules.gap: per pair: mean d over the reuse side's seeds minus mean d over the new side's (experiments/method_table/plot_final.score)
rules.apart: every seed of one side beyond every seed of the other, at least 2 seeds a side (plot_final.score); else 'no call' or 'one value a side'
rules.size-matched: the larger side (E187 m67.json .pairs[pair].larger) read again at dW times c (m67.json .pairs[pair].c); the smaller side keeps its as-built d
rules.missing: a pair with any side unread or a nan d is drawn x (not run) and counts as not gap > 0

predictions.P1: As built: gap > 0 on at least 7 of the 9 built pairs (the user's expectation, 2026-11-17)
predictions.P2: Size-matched: gap > 0 on at least 7 of the 9 built pairs

edge_cases.base against itself: change energy 0, d nan: the self control is read on latent counts and relative norms only; a nan d can never count toward P1 or P2
edge_cases.do-nothing state: the random update enters no gap. If both sides of every pair read like it (d near 0), P1 counts only the sign of near-zero gaps and could pass by chance (each about 1 in 2; 7 of 9 by chance about 9%); the apart count, which a pair of near-zero sides cannot reach unless the seed spread is tiny, is reported beside it and is the stricter read
edge_cases.two seeds a side: e53_lowercase_cipher reuse and e54_own new have 2: the apart rule applies (needs at least 2)
edge_cases.no fine-tune-specific latent: the fine-tune-specific part is 0 (an empty group sums to 0), d = shared part; defined
edge_cases.shared states: e54/elicit_s0..s4 serve e54_matched and e54_own, c3/cipher_s0..s7 serve both c3 pairs: one crosscoder each, read in both pairs
edge_cases.negative parts: a group's part can be below 0 (it points against the change); d is not clipped; the colour is capped at 1 as on the scorecard
